assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs with transformative effects on type 2 diabetes and obesity, a rare case of basic hormone biology becoming a broad therapy with documented cardiometabolic outcome benefits. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are very high; the central-appetite action of GLP-1 also connects to neural circuit control of feeding.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 as the key incretin), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and therapeutic translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide forms) form a plausible three-person configuration; Knudsen's contribution is more drug-development oriented and would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Therapies have been clinically deployed at scale for years with large independent outcome trials, so the field is mature and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener and others for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is contested and the supplied names may not capture it fully.
Drug-development contributions (Knudsen, industry teams) versus basic discovery make a fair three-person split difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience cell-type-specific, millisecond-precision control of activity, reshaping circuit analysis across systems including motor circuits. The invention is original, clear and has had exceptional, field-wide methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal implementation (Boyden, Deisseroth) are distinct steps; a laureate set must choose among six credited names. Hegemann for the molecular tool with Boyden and Deisseroth for neuronal use is one reasonable configuration, leaving Nagel, Bamberg and Miesenböck unrecognized.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by thousands of independent studies and now entering clinical vision restoration; interpretation is stable and timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded and contested, with more than three strong claimants.
Mostly a tool rather than a disease mechanism; clinical impact is still early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with strong conceptual originality and clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CD19 CAR-T translation with costimulation), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and design principles) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) are a defensible trio; Eshhar and others who originated chimeric receptors are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up confirm durable benefit, though toxicity, relapse and solid-tumor limits remain.
uncertainties: Pioneering chimeric-receptor work by others is not in the credited names.
Long-term outcomes and solid-tumor efficacy are still incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined the main pathway for cytosolic DNA sensing, linking innate immunity to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer. Conceptually clear and widely generalizing.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAMP second messenger and cGAS identification, with Sun) and Barber (STING identification) are the decisive contributors; Ishikawa and Wu are less central than Sun and Chen for cGAS, though the pair of Chen with Barber captures the pathway most cleanly.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is firmly confirmed and broadly reproduced; therapeutic translation remains early, so recognition rests on mechanism rather than clinical success.
uncertainties: Therapeutic modulation has not yet shown clear clinical benefit.
Fair credit between Barber, Ishikawa and the Chen laboratory for STING and between Sun and Wu for cGAS is partially unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of strongly reduced precancer and cancer incidence. This is a clear, highly consequential preventive medicine discovery.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (VLP development and immunogenicity) and Frazer (VLP vaccine concept and early work) are a natural trio, though Zhou and others in Frazer's group and zur Hausen-related work have overlapping credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long-term population effectiveness data across countries; the 2008 recognition of HPV discovery by the prize does not preclude vaccine recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap of credit with other VLP developers outside the supplied names.
Prior prize for HPV-cancer linkage may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identified the central growth and nutrient-sensing kinase, with broad consequences for metabolism, aging, immunity and cancer, and clinical use of rapalogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined its function; Sabatini identified mTOR and mTORC1 regulators in mammals. Schreiber's rapamycin-target chemistry is also important but a two-person prize is cleaner.
assessment.maturity: Foundational and extensively confirmed; clinical impact is real but moderate relative to the biological reach.
uncertainties: Rapamycin target discovery was shared across several groups (Heitman, Hall, Sabatini, Sabers, Brown), so credit is crowded.
Allegations affecting Sabatini's standing may influence committee willingness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for SMA turned a lethal childhood motor neuron disease into a treatable one, with strong rational design from SMN2 splicing mechanism to drug. Clear and clinically powerful, with obvious interest to motor system disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are well matched; other contributors such as Singh and Hua are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved drug with years of follow-up, though long-term durability and comparison to gene therapy are still developing.
uncertainties: Credit for foundational SMN2 biology (Lefebvre, Melki, Monani) lies outside the supplied names.
Late-treatment outcomes and long-term durability remain incompletely known.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chaperonin-assisted folding established that proteins fold in assisted compartments in cells, a foundational principle for proteostasis, neurodegeneration and protein quality control.
assessment.attribution: Horwich and Hartl jointly demonstrated chaperonin-mediated folding in vivo and in vitro, a clean two-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: Long confirmed and textbook; recognition is not premature, but direct medical impact is indirect compared with higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: Contributions of Georgopoulos and Ellis on GroEL and chaperone concepts are outside the credited names.
